title: Poverty reduction has stalled globally while social protection expands unevenly across groups and places
source_unit: United Nations SDG Indicators, 2026 Sustainable Development Goals Report, Goal 1: No poverty
geography: Global and regional SDG monitoring, with country and population-group comparisons where data are available

denominator.unit: global population measured against the $3.00/day 2021 PPP extreme-poverty line

extreme_poverty_rate.unit: percent of the global population estimated to live in extreme poverty in 2026

people_in_extreme_poverty.unit: million people estimated to live in extreme poverty in 2026

2030_projected_rate.unit: percent of the global population projected to remain in extreme poverty in 2030 at the current trajectory

sub_saharan_concentration.unit: percent of the world's extreme poor concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa

observations.method: UN SDG indicator monitoring using global and regional poverty estimates and projections based on the $3.00/day 2021 PPP line.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate depends on survey coverage, purchasing-power revisions, national accounts projections, and the chosen poverty line; the 2030 figure is a trajectory projection rather than a forecast of policy outcomes.
observations.subgroup: People in extreme poverty, sub-Saharan African populations, fragile and conflict-affected settings, and regions with different recovery paths.
observations.counterinterpretation: Global averages can conceal substantial country-level progress and do not show whether households move temporarily or persistently below the poverty line.

denominator.unit: global population and population groups covered by at least one social-protection benefit

any_benefit_coverage.unit: percent of the global population covered by at least one social-protection benefit

unprotected_population.unit: billion people without any form of social protection

children_family_benefit.unit: percent of children receiving a family benefit

unemployed_protection.unit: percent of unemployed people covered by unemployment protection

old_age_coverage.unit: percent of people above retirement age receiving old-age protection

observations.method: UN SDG indicator compilation of social-protection coverage by population group and benefit type.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage means receipt of at least one benefit and does not establish adequacy, duration, take-up barriers, real purchasing power, or protection against a specific shock.
observations.subgroup: Children, mothers with newborns, people with severe disabilities, workers, unemployed people, older persons, and vulnerable populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage expansion can coexist with inadequate benefit levels; low group coverage may reflect eligibility rules, labor informality, administrative gaps, or measurement differences.

denominator.unit: employed population measured against the $3.00/day 2021 PPP line

working_poor.unit: million workers living in extreme poverty

working_poverty_rate.unit: percent of employed people living in extreme poverty

sub_saharan_and_ldc_rate.unit: approximately percent working-poverty rate in sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries

youth_risk.value: young people aged 15-24 are more than twice as likely as adults to be working poor

observations.method: UN SDG labor and poverty indicator monitoring by region, development grouping, and age.
observations.uncertainty: Working-poverty estimates depend on employment and household income measurement and do not distinguish job quality, hours, household composition, or informal-work dynamics in every country.
observations.subgroup: Young workers, adults, workers in sub-Saharan Africa, least developed countries, landlocked developing countries, and other regions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Employment can reduce poverty without eliminating vulnerability; income support, productivity, hours, household size, and public services shape whether work produces security.

denominator.unit: countries or areas with comparable pro-poor public-spending data in at least one sector

bottom_quintile_combined_reach.unit: average share of combined education, health, and direct-transfer spending reaching the poorest 20 percent

cash_transfer_reach.unit: average share of direct cash and near-cash transfers reaching the poorest 20 percent

education_reach.unit: average share of education spending reaching the poorest 20 percent

poverty_reduction_oda_change.unit: percent change in poverty-reduction ODA grants between 2023 and 2024

poverty_reduction_oda_2024.unit: billion dollars in poverty-reduction ODA grants in 2024

observations.method: UN SDG monitoring of pro-poor public spending and official development assistance grants.
observations.uncertainty: Spending incidence is not the same as service quality or outcome impact; country comparability and sector coverage vary, and ODA changes do not directly measure all external finance or domestic policy responses.
observations.subgroup: The poorest 20 percent, users of education and health services, recipients of transfers, low-income countries, and communities affected by aid-funded services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate spending can have long-term benefits that incidence measures miss, while highly targeted transfers may not substitute for universal, high-quality public services.

related_sources.claim: UN 2026 Sustainable Development Goals Report provides the broader indicator context.
World Bank State of Social Protection Report provides complementary coverage and adequacy analysis.

boundary: This record adds a current SDG monitoring route linking extreme poverty, working poverty, social-protection coverage, public spending incidence, aid flows, conflict, climate shocks, and living costs. It is aggregate indicator evidence, not household panel data, respondent-level benefit histories, a causal evaluation of social-protection programs, or proof that coverage is adequate.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN SDG Goal 1 2026 page was reviewed for global poverty estimates, 2030 trajectory, social-protection group coverage, working poverty, public spending incidence, and poverty-reduction ODA changes.
